messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: nested / non nested models?
parts:
Leonhard--
It is confusing that you have three "cfa" statements, but two of them use the same lavaan model syntax. Which of the two anova statements produces the error message?
--Ed Rigdon

On Mon, May 23, 2016 at 4:19 PM, <leonhard...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear all,

I am comparing models using the anova function (see below), but at the second difference test it tells me that:

Error in lav_test_diff_af_h1(m1 = m1, m0 = m0) : 
  lavaan ERROR: unconstrained parameter set is not the same in m0 and m1

However, if I am not mistaken a model with no correlated errors is nested in the model with correlated errors.
Could you tell me why this error occurs?

# Models

three.factor <- '
  LV1 =~ MV1 + MV2 + MV3 + MV4 + MV5
  LV2 =~ MV6 + MV7 + MV8 + MV9 + MV10 + MV11 
  LV3 =~ MV12 + MV13 + MV14
  '

three.factor.correlated.error.89 <- '
  LV1 =~ MV1 + MV2 + MV3 + MV4 + MV5
  LV2 =~ MV6 + MV7 + MV8 + MV9 + MV10 + MV11 
  LV3 =~ MV12 + MV13 + MV14

  MV1 ~~ MV2
'

# CFA

WLSMV.three.factor.no.cov.cfa  <- cfa(three.factor, data = TS, estimator = "WLSMV", orthogonal = T, mimic = "Mplus")
summary(WLSMV.three.factor.no.cov.cfa, standardized = T, fit.measures = T, modindices = T)

WLSMV.three.factor.cov.cfa  <- cfa(three.factor, data = TS, estimator = "WLSMV", orthogonal = F, mimic = "Mplus")
summary(WLSMV.three.factor.cov.cfa, standardized = T, fit.measures = T, modindices = T)

WLSMV.three.factor.cov.correlated.error.89.cfa  <- cfa(three.factor.correlated.error.89, data = TS, estimator = "WLSMV", orthogonal = F, mimic = "Mplus")
summary(WLSMV.three.factor.cov.correlated.error.89.cfa, standardized = T, fit.measures = T, modindices = T)

# ANOVA

anova(WLSMV.three.factor.no.cov.cfa, WLSMV.three.factor.cov.cfa)
anova(WLSMV.three.factor.cov.cfa, WLSMV.three.factor.cov.correlated.error.89.cfa)

messages.author: 8ec990fe01b9d806
messages.subject: Re: nested / non nested models?
parts:
Hi,

It means that the models are not nested in the parameter sense: m0 is not a subset of m1. I would advice you to check the estimated parameters in your model. The scaling or something else might cause these kind of problems.

Mariska
